newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end weaker in quiet pre-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end weaker in quiet pre-holiday trade.

text.p: Canadian bonds ended much weaker at an early market close on Monday, with some investors winding up long positions ahead of tomorrow's Canada Day market holiday, analysts said.

"Tomorrow we have U.S. data coming out, so I don't think anybody wanted to be long ahead of that, plus you have FOMC meeting," said Harvinder Kalirai, Canadian analyst with financial analysis firm IDEA.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$1.36 to C$113.95 to yield 6.892 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 29/32 to yield 6.82 percent. The spread between the bonds widened to seven basis points from five basis points at Friday's close.

The Toronto bond market closed early at 1200 EDT/1600 GMT on Monday ahead of the Canada Day public and market holiday. The move essentially means an early close for the entire Canadian bond market because most trading is done in Toronto.

Analysts said much of the market's tone was set by weaker U.S. Treasuries, which softened following the release of stronge economic data there. Canadian trading activity was light with many market players absent ahead of the holiday.

"There's rumors of some big Canadian seller of bonds. I don't know. Not many people saw it so I can't confirm it and it's very thin. The U.S. trading obviously didn't help at all," said one corporate bond trader with a bank-owned brokerage.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.81 to C$106.57 to yield 6.345 percent, compared to its U.S. equivalent which fell 19/32 to yield 6.54 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 20 basis points from 22 basis points at Friday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.22 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.19 percent.
